candidates.introducingSubject: internal/grpcutil: remove FullMatchWithRegex to prevent data race (#9134)
candidates.reviewedPathsExcludedReason: Tests only; the existing corpus keeps reviewedPaths production-only. The updated unit tests also spell out the new anchoring convention.
candidates.disjointnessProof: internal/xds/rbac/matchers.go is not among the five reviewed paths and is not modified by 39f16539 at all (git show --name-only lists 10 files, none of them rbac/matchers.go).

evidenceCommits.subject: xds: ensure full-string matching for RBAC Filter rules (#9148)
quotes: This PR fixes a regression introduced in #9134 where xDS SafeRegexMatch configurations were performing partial matches instead of the full-string matches as earlier in RBAC.
PullRequest #9134 removed grpcutil.FullMatchWithRegex in favor of regexp.MatchString. In Go, MatchString performs a partial match unless the regex is explicitly anchored with ^ and $.

The regression was caught by psm-interop tests where an RBAC DENY rule was bypassed due to a partial match in an preceding ALLOW rule. RBAC test started failing continuously after May 20 (Commit time)
evidenceCommits.linkVerification: The introducing commit's own subject ends with '(#9134)', so the PR number in the evidence body resolves to 39f16539 exactly.

expectedImpact.severityRationale: Impact: control defeated - the RBAC engine is itself the thing that grants and denies, and a caller-supplied header value is accepted as matching a principal rule it does not match. Reachability: conditional - the deployment's xDS policy has to use a SafeRegexMatch header rule. Matrix: control defeated x conditional = high.
expectedImpact.semanticSummary: newHeaderMatcher compiles the xDS SafeRegexMatch pattern with plain regexp.Compile and hands the result to NewHeaderRegexMatcher, whose Match now asks the pattern itself whether it matches and no longer requires the match to cover the whole header value. An unanchored pattern therefore matches on any substring, so an RBAC rule for principal "admin" also matches "never-admin": a DENY rule can be evaded and an ALLOW rule can authorise a peer it was not written for.

reachability.label: caller-of-changed-symbol
reachability.explanation: Q imports the changed package (internalmatcher "google.golang.org/grpc/internal/xds/matcher") and calls NewHeaderRegexMatcher, the constructor that sits three lines above the Match body the diff rewrote. A reviewer who asks 'who else builds one of these matchers' reaches Q in one hop. The changed line itself is the Match method, not the constructor, so the link is constructor-to-method rather than a direct call of a changed function.

localPlausibility.note: Read alone the diff is a clean refactor: it deletes a helper that mutated shared regexp state via re.Longest() (a real data race) and preserves full-string semantics by anchoring at every compile site the commit knows about. Nothing in the diff is wrong. The defect is only that the set of compile sites is larger than the diff.

flagged.text: // CompileSafeRegex attempts to compile the provided pattern as a regular expression. It first compiles the unanchored pattern to catch syntax errors and then compiles and returns the explicitly anchored pattern to guarantee full-string matching.
flagged.rationale: States the contract of the new helper. Names no caller, no file outside the diff, and no failure. It does tell the reviewer that anchoring is now a compile-time responsibility, which is the reasoning step the case is meant to test rather than the answer to it.

flagged.text: // FullMatchWithRegex returns whether the full text matches the regex provided.
flagged.rationale: The deleted function's own doc comment; the same information is visible from its body.

disclosureCheck.overall: No advisory wording, no CVE/GHSA id, no comment naming the impacted file. Needs a human sign-off on the first item.

candidates.notes: internal/xds/httpfilter/extconfig.go, the second file the evidence commit repairs, did not exist at 39f16539 and must not be listed as impacted. internal/xds/xdsclient/xdsresource/unmarshal_rds.go:427 still uses plain regexp.Compile at head, but that pattern feeds a regex *rewrite*, not a matcher, and the file is inside P anyway.

candidates.introducingSubject: Refs #36644 -- Applied default ordering after union().
candidates.disjointnessProof: 087bb9e8 modifies exactly two files, django/db/models/query.py and tests/queries/test_qs_combinators.py. django/db/models/sql/query.py is a different module and is untouched.

evidenceCommits.subject: Fixed #37097 -- Made Query.clear_ordering() clear ordering on combined queries also.
quotes: (That commit drove more traffic into an error that would have been reachable only with an explicit order_by() after each union().)
evidenceCommits.linkVerification: Full sha of the introducing commit is quoted verbatim in the evidence body.

expectedImpact.severityRationale: Impact: signalled or bounded - the query fails loudly at the database rather than returning a wrong row set. Reachability: remote - a nested union, used as the right-hand side of an __in lookup, restricted to a column other than the ordering column. Matrix: signalled x remote = low. NOTE: a low expectation is only matchable by a candidate the engine itself rates medium or above (spec 17, Expectations Per Case).
expectedImpact.semanticSummary: clear_ordering resets order_by, extra_order_by and default_ordering on the receiver only, never descending into self.combined_queries, though as_sql in the same class does that loop. A caller stripping ordering before embedding a query as a subquery - In.get_prep_lookup - thus leaves nested union arms ordering by Meta.ordering. The compiler appends that arm's ordering column to its select list, so the outer union's arms no longer have matching column counts and the database rejects the query.

reachability.label: attribute-owner
reachability.explanation: The single changed line assigns to default_ordering on an instance of the Query class that Q defines, so Q is one hop away by following the mutated attribute to its owner. Confirming the failure needs a second hop the diff does not point at: django/db/models/lookups.py, where In.get_prep_lookup calls clear_ordering on a subquery and relies on it having cleared everything.

localPlausibility.note: The diff is one added line that restores the model's default ordering to a queryset built by union(), immediately after the surrounding code deliberately cleared ordering 'so they can be reapplied'. There is nothing in the diff to object to.

disclosureCheck.overall: Clean. The only comment in the hunk is pre-existing context ('# Clear limits and ordering so they can be reapplied') and is unchanged.

candidates.notes: Best of the five on local plausibility - a one-line addition with no visible hint - and worst on severity, since the failure is a loud database error and the rubric caps that at low.

candidates.splitRationale: Introducing commit is 2025-05-23, before the manifest's declared training cutoff of 2026-01-01, so it cannot be held-out.

evidenceCommits.subject: Fixed #36751 -- Fixed empty filtered aggregation crash over annotated queryset.
quotes: The replace_expressions method was innapropriately dealing with falsey but not None source expressions causing them to also be potentially evaluated when __bool__ was invoked (e.g. QuerySet.__bool__ evaluates the queryset).

The changes introduced in b8e5a8a9a2, which were to deal with a similar issue, surfaced the problem as aggregation over an annotated queryset requires an inlining (or pushdown) of aggregate references which is achieved through replace_expressions.
evidenceCommits.linkVerification: Full sha of the introducing commit is quoted verbatim in the evidence body.

expectedImpact.severityRationale: Impact: silently wrong - a child expression that is present but falsey is replaced by None while rebuilding the tree, and the truthiness test itself can execute a queryset (QuerySet.__bool__ evaluates) during what is supposed to be a pure rewrite. Reachability: conditional - needs an aggregate pushed down over an annotated queryset. Matrix: silently wrong x conditional = medium.
expectedImpact.semanticSummary: replace_expressions rebuilds children as 'expr.replace_expressions(replacements) if expr else None', discriminating on truthiness where only None means absent. A child that is present but falsey is silently replaced by None, and testing it runs the child's __bool__, which for a queryset child executes a query. An aggregate whose filter is an empty Q now arrives as a real, empty, falsey filter node: the pushdown drops it to None and compiling the filter then dereferences it.

reachability.label: whole-repo-search
reachability.explanation: Q defines the base class of the class the diff changes, but the diff never mentions replace_expressions or source expressions. Reaching Q means noticing that self.filter is a source expression, and then searching the repository for code that inspects source expressions by truthiness. There is no import edge or call in the diff that leads there.

localPlausibility.note: The diff replaces 'filter and AggregateFilter(filter)' with an explicit None test and drops a now-redundant re-resolution of the filter. Read alone it is a strict improvement: it removes a truthiness bug. The contract it changes is that an empty filter used to collapse to None and now does not.

disclosureCheck.overall: Clean. No comments added or removed in the reviewed file.

candidates.notes: The introducing commit is itself a bugfix, which is the ideal texture for this fixture type: the reviewer cannot fall back on 'this change looks sloppy'.

evidenceCommits.subject: Fixed #36433 -- Fixed constraint validation crash when condition uses a ForeignKey attname.
evidenceCommits.linkVerification: Full sha quoted verbatim; the fix adds field_map[field.attname] = value in django/db/models/base.py and touches no other production file.

evidenceCommits.subject: Fixed #36580 -- Fixed constraint validation crash when condition uses a ForeignObject.
evidenceCommits.linkVerification: Full sha quoted verbatim; the fix widens the same loop in django/db/models/base.py from local_concrete_fields to local_fields.

expectedImpact.severityRationale: Impact: signalled or bounded - full_clean raises an unexpected exception type instead of validating, which the caller sees. Reachability: conditional - one further condition, a constraint whose condition names a foreign key's attname. Matrix: signalled x conditional = low.
expectedImpact.semanticSummary: _get_field_expression_map keys the map it returns by field.name only, so the entry for a foreign key is 'author' and never 'author_id'. Constraint validation resolves the condition against exactly this map and now lets a FieldError from an unresolvable name escape rather than treating it as 'cannot check here'. Any model carrying a constraint whose condition is written against a foreign key's attname therefore raises FieldError out of full_clean instead of either validating or skipping.

expectedImpact.severityRationale: Same bands as the sibling expectation: a visible wrong exception out of full_clean, gated on one further condition (a multi-column relation named in a constraint condition).
expectedImpact.semanticSummary: The map is built by iterating meta.local_concrete_fields and reading getattr(self, field.attname), so a relation spanning several columns - which is not a concrete field and has no single attname - contributes no entry at all. A constraint condition naming such a relation cannot be resolved against the map, and because the validate path no longer absorbs the resulting FieldError, full_clean raises it instead of checking the constraint.

reachability.label: callee-of-changed-code
reachability.explanation: The changed function's first statement calls instance._get_field_expression_map, defined in Q, and Q's return value is what the condition is checked against. One hop, and the diff names the call. What the diff does not show is which names that map omits, which is the whole expectation.

localPlausibility.verdict: plausible, with a caveat the human should weigh
localPlausibility.note: The diff removes a try/except FieldError: pass around the condition check and replaces it with an explicit _expression_refs_exclude precheck. That is a legitimate cleanup and the diff does not say what the swallowed FieldError was for. But a reviewer can see an exception handler disappear and ask 'did the precheck cover every case it covered' without leaving the diff. The answer still requires reading Q, so the expectation remains out-of-diff, but this case is less purely local than the other four.

flagged.text: # Ignore constraints with excluded fields in condition.
flagged.rationale: Describes the added guard. Says nothing about FieldError, about name resolution, or about base.py.

candidates.notes: Two independent upstream fixes to the same file six months apart, which makes this the only proposed case with two separately evidenced expectations.

candidates.introducingSubject: Refs #29984 -- Made QuerySet.iterator() without chunk_size raise ValueError after prefetch_related().
candidates.reviewedPathsExcludedReason: Docs and tests. The release note states the new hard failure in prose.
candidates.disjointnessProof: 1391356276 modifies django/db/models/query.py plus two docs files and one test file. Neither impacted path is among them.

evidenceCommits.subject: Fixed #35159 -- Fixed dumpdata crash when base querysets use prefetch_related().
quotes: Regression in 139135627650ed6aaaf4c755b82c3bd43f2b8f51 following deprecation in edbf930287cb72e9afab1f7208c24b1146b0c4ec.
evidenceCommits.linkVerification: Full sha quoted verbatim; the fix passes a chunk_size at the impacted call site and touches no other production file.

evidenceCommits.subject: Fixed #35238 -- Fixed database serialization crash when base managers use prefetch_related().
evidenceCommits.linkVerification: Full sha quoted verbatim; the fix passes a chunk_size at the impacted call site and touches no other production file.

expectedImpact.severityRationale: Impact: signalled or bounded - the management command aborts with a visible exception. Reachability: conditional - one further condition, a model whose default or base manager attaches prefetch_related lookups. Matrix: signalled x conditional = low.
expectedImpact.semanticSummary: get_objects streams each model's rows with queryset.iterator() and passes no chunk_size, which was previously merely discouraged for a queryset carrying prefetch lookups and is now refused outright. A model whose manager applies prefetch_related - which dumpdata neither controls nor strips, since it uses the model's own manager - therefore makes the whole dump abort with ValueError before writing anything, rather than dumping that model's rows.

expectedImpact.severityRationale: Same bands: a visible exception, gated on one further condition (a base manager that prefetches).
expectedImpact.semanticSummary: serialize_db_to_string walks every model through model._base_manager.using(...).order_by(pk) and drains it with queryset.iterator() and no chunk_size, a call that is now refused whenever the queryset carries prefetch lookups. A project whose base manager prefetches makes database serialization raise ValueError, so the serialized_rollback path that depends on it cannot capture the database state at all.

reachability.label: whole-repo-search
reachability.explanation: Neither impacted file is imported by the diff, imports the diff's module by name at the call site, or is referenced anywhere in the change. The only route is to take the newly refused call shape - iterator() with no chunk_size - and search the repository for call sites, then decide for each whether its queryset can carry prefetch lookups. This is exactly the 'reachable only by whole-repo search' class.

localPlausibility.verdict: plausible - the strongest of the five
localPlausibility.note: The change completes a documented deprecation on schedule: a warning that had already announced its own replacement becomes the ValueError it announced. There is no defect in the diff under any reading.

flagged.text:
# When the deprecation ends, replace with:
# raise ValueError(
#     'chunk_size must be provided when using '
#     'QuerySet.iterator() after prefetch_related().'
# )
flagged.rationale: A removed commented-out draft of the change being made. It describes the diff itself, not the callers, and names nothing outside the file.

disclosureCheck.overall: Clean, but note the excluded docs/releases/5.0.txt would have described the new hard failure in prose - keep it out of reviewedPaths.

candidates.notes: Age is the weakness here: a 2023 django commit is almost certainly in training data, so this case measures reachability more honestly on a fresh model than on the current one.
